mainTopic: The sources for giving the קנס to forbidden girls, and the תנאים who limit it based on ״ולו תהיה לאשה״
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: a girl gets the קנס even during the years when her father can still sell her. The גמרא then asks why girls who are forbidden to the man get the קנס at all, since the פסוק says ״ולו תהיה לאשה״. ריש לקיש learns them from the three mentions of ״נערה״, and רב פפא learns them from the three mentions of ״בתולה״. The גמרא asks why each one avoided the other's source. It explains that ״הנערה״ is needed for אביי's rule (no קנס if the girl died) and that ״הבתולות״ is needed for a גזירה שוה. It then shows that each sage needs both of these teachings, so it concludes that all six words are counted together, leaving two words to include girls forbidden by a לאו and by כרת. Next the גמרא brings a ברייתא our משנה rejects: שמעון התימני limits the קנס to a woman whose קידושין works, and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא limits it to a woman he may keep. רבי זירא says they differ over a ממזרת or a נתינה. The גמרא asks what the difference would be according to רבי עקיבא, and answers with an אלמנה and a כהן גדול, following רבי סימאי. It then asks the same question according to רבי ישבב's report of רבי עקיבא, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A fine can be paid even when the girl can be sold
steps.stepSummary: This line closes the earlier discussion: the קנס applies even during the period when the father can still sell his daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a fine even in a place where there is sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its previous discussion with a short conclusion. A girl gets the קנס even during the years when her father can still sell her as a maidservant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being sellable (מכר) and being entitled to a fine (קנס) do not cancel each other out. Both can apply to the same girl during the same years.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed fine set by the Torah (here, fifty silver pieces)
Sale: a father's right to sell his young daughter as a maidservant
Literally 'in the place of'; here it means in a situation where

steps.whatToRemember: The fine and the father's right to sell can exist side by side for the same girl.

phrases.english: There is a fine even in a place where there is sale.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a sentence from the earlier discussion. He means a girl young enough to be sold still gets the fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that came before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The קנס applies even during the years when the father has the right to sell her.

steps.title: Why should forbidden girls get the fine at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: the פסוק ״ולו תהיה לאשה״ suggests the fine applies only to a girl he is allowed to marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these girls entitled to the fine? Why should they be? I read here, ״And to him she shall be as a wife״, which means a wife who is fit for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the משנה's ruling that girls who are forbidden to the man still receive the קנס. The פסוק seems to limit the fine to girls he could actually marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: About the אונס, the Torah says he must marry the girl he forced. That suggests the whole section, including the fine, is only about a girl who is fit to become his wife. The girls in the משנה are forbidden to him, so they should be left out.

keyTerms.meaning: People entitled to receive the fine
'I read here': this פסוק should apply here
Fit for him, meaning someone he is allowed to marry

phrases.english: And are these entitled to the fine?
phrases.notes: 'These' are the girls listed in the משנה who are forbidden to the man.

phrases.english: But why? I read here:
“And to him she shall be as a wife,”
a wife who is fit for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the משנה's list of forbidden girls.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that girls forbidden by a לאו or by כרת still receive the קנס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ״ולו תהיה לאשה״ seems to limit the whole אונס section, fine included, to a girl fit to marry him.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: three mentions of ״נערה״ include them
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש counts ״נערה״, ״נערה״, ״הנערה״. One teaches the basic law, one adds girls forbidden by a לאו, and one adds girls forbidden by כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: ״young woman״, ״young woman״, ״the young woman״. One is for the basic law, one includes those forbidden by a prohibition, and one includes those forbidden under penalty of כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question by finding extra words in the פסוקים of אונס. Those extra words bring forbidden girls into the קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra ״נערה״ words show that the Torah wants to widen the fine beyond the simple case. That widening outweighs the hint from ״ולו תהיה לאשה״, so girls forbidden by a לאו or by כרת still get the קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: For itself: teaching the basic law
To include, to bring in an extra case
Relations forbidden by a negative commandment (a לאו)
Relations whose punishment is כרת

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
“Young woman,” “young woman,” “the young woman.”
phrases.notes: From the אונס פסוקים in דברים 22:28–29. The extra 'the' counts as a third mention.

phrases.english: One is for itself,
and one is to include those forbidden by prohibitions,
and one is to include those forbidden under penalty of karet.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Derivation from extra words in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״ולו תהיה לאשה״ leaves out every girl he cannot marry.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra mentions of ״נערה״ include girls forbidden by a לאו or by כרת.

steps.title: רב פפא: three mentions of ״בתולה״ include them
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a different source: ״בתולה״, ״בתולות״, ״הבתולות״ in the פסוקים about the seducer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: ״virgin״, ״virgins״, ״the virgins״. One is for the basic law, one includes those forbidden by a prohibition, and one includes those forbidden under penalty of כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא reaches the same result as ריש לקיש but uses a different set of extra words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method and the result are the same: three mentions, the first for the basic law and two to include forbidden girls. Only the source changes, from ״נערה״ to ״בתולה״.

keyTerms.meaning: A virgin
A seducer, whose case is in שמות 22

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא does not disagree with the ruling. Both agree that forbidden girls get the קנס; they only argue about which words teach it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
“Virgin,” “virgins,” “the virgins.”
One is for itself,
and one is to include those forbidden by prohibitions,
and one is to include those forbidden under penalty of karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 2's question, using a different source than ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra mentions of ״בתולה״ include girls forbidden by a לאו or by כרת.

steps.title: Why didn't רב פפא use ריש לקיש's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב פפא needed a different source instead of using ״נערה״ like ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא, what is his reason that he did not say like ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב פפא chose a different source. This sets up the next step, which explains what ״נערה״ is needed for in his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״נערה״ already works, choosing ״בתולה״ instead suggests that רב פפא needs ״נערה״ for something else. The גמרא wants to find out what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Did not say like (did not follow someone's approach)

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa, what is the reason
that he did not say as Reish Lakish did?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב פָּפָּא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers given in steps 3 and 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב פפא does not use the ״נערה״ source.

steps.title: רב פפא needs ״הנערה״ for אביי's rule about a girl who died
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא uses ״הנערה״ for אביי's rule: if the girl died before he paid, he is פטור, because the fine goes to the father of a living נערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that verse for אביי's teaching. אביי said: if he forced her and she died, he is exempt, as it says, ״and he shall give to the father of the young woman״. That means to the father of a young woman, and not to the father of a dead woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב פפא is already using the extra ״הנערה״ for a different law, which comes from אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'to her father'. Instead it says 'the father of the נערה', which teaches that she must still be alive for the fine to be paid. Since רב פפא uses that word for this rule, he has to learn the inclusion of forbidden girls from ״בתולה״ instead.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (the word is already used for another teaching)
He had relations with her
Exempt from paying
A dead woman

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's rule: if the girl died before he paid, there is no קנס, because the פסוק says 'the father of the נערה'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of learning from extra words: one word cannot teach two separate laws. Once ״הנערה״ is used for one law, a different source is needed for the other.

phrases.english: He needs that for what Abaye said.
As Abaye said:
If he had relations with her by force and she died, he is exempt,
as it says: “And he shall give to the father of the young woman.”
To the father of a young woman, and not to the father of a dead woman.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא uses ״הנערה״ for אביי's rule that there is no קנס if the girl died, so he takes the inclusion of forbidden girls from ״בתולה״.

steps.title: Why didn't ריש לקיש use רב פפא's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now turns the question around and asks why ריש לקיש did not learn from ״בתולה״ like רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש, why didn't he say it like רב פפא?
steps.whatsHappening: Just as the גמרא asked about רב פפא, it now asks about ריש לקיש. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 we learned that רב פפא needs ״הנערה״ for אביי's rule. Now the גמרא wants to know what ריש לקיש needs the ״בתולה״ words for.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish, what is the reason
that he did not say it like Rav Pappa?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror question to step 5, now aimed at ריש לקיש
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What ריש לקיש uses the ״בתולה״ words for, if not for including forbidden girls

steps.title: ריש לקיש needs the ״בתולה״ words for a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש needs the ״בתולה״ words for a גזירה שוה that ties together the מפתה's fine and the מוהר הבתולות of the אונס.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that for a גזירה שוה, as a ברייתא teaches: ״He shall weigh money like the dowry of the virgins״. This fine should be like the dowry of the virgins, and the dowry of the virgins should be like this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ריש לקיש is already using the ״בתולה״ words for something else: a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא links the two cases in both directions. The מפתה pays fifty, the same amount as the אונס, and the אונס's payment is in the same coin as the מפתה's. Since the ״בתולות״ words are busy with this link, ריש לקיש cannot also use them to include forbidden girls.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (this word is already used for something else)
Learning one case from another through a shared word
The set payment for a virgin (fifty, as stated by the אונס)

phrases.english: That one is needed by him for a gezeira shava.
As it was taught: “He shall weigh money like the dowry of the virgins,”
that this should be like the dowry of the virgins,
phrases.notes: "This" means the seducer's fine. It equals the fifty the אונס pays.

phrases.english: and the dowry of the virgins like this.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ריש לקיש uses the ״בתולות״ words for the גזירה שוה linking the מפתה and the אונס

steps.title: Each sage also needs the other's derivation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges both answers: ריש לקיש also needs a word for אביי, and רב פפא also needs a word for the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But ריש לקיש also needs a word for אביי's rule. And רב פפא also needs a word for the גזירה שוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the two answers do not fully work. Each sage also has to account for the other's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages accept אביי's rule and the גזירה שוה, so each one has to use up words for both. ריש לקיש uses one ״נערה״ for the basic law and one for אביי, which leaves only one word, not two, for the לאוין and the כריתות. The same thing happens to רב פפא once he uses a ״בתולה״ word for the גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Also
For what אביי said (the girl who died before payment)

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ נָמֵי, מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְאַבָּיֵי.
phrases.english: And Reish Lakish too needs it for Abaye's teaching.
phrases.notes: This is אביי's rule from step 6: if she died before he paid, he is פטור.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב פָּפָּא נָמֵי, מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לִגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה!
phrases.english: And Rav Pappa too needs it for the gezeira shava!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ נָמֵי, מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answers given in steps 6 and 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The answers in steps 6 and 8, which assume that each sage's own three words are free to include forbidden girls.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each sage needs both אביי's rule and the גזירה שוה. After the basic law and the extra teaching he also needs, his three words leave only one, not enough to include both חייבי לאוין and חייבי כריתות.

steps.title: Six words: both sages use all of them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that there are six words in total, and both sages divide them the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, six words are written: ״נערה״, ״נערה״, ״הנערה״, ״בתולה״, ״בתולות״, ״הבתולות״. Two teach the basic laws, one teaches אביי's rule, and one teaches the גזירה שוה. Two are left over: one includes girls forbidden by a לאו, and one includes girls forbidden by כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem by counting all six words together. Both sages really agree on how to use them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of each sage drawing from only one set of three words, all six are pooled. After four words are used (two for the basic laws, one for אביי, one for the גזירה שוה), two remain. These two include girls forbidden by a לאו and girls forbidden by כרת. So ריש לקיש and רב פפא do not truly argue.

keyTerms.meaning: Six words/verses
For the basic law itself
Are left over
Women forbidden by a לאו
Women forbidden with כרת

steps.whatToRemember: There are six words in all. Two teach the basic laws, one teaches אביי's rule, and one teaches the גזירה שוה. The last two add girls forbidden by a לאו and by כרת. This matches the משנה: the קנס is paid even for forbidden girls.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think ריש לקיש and רב פפא still disagree. In the end they share all six words the same way.

phrases.english: Rather: six words are written!
phrases.notes: Read this as a statement, not a question: count all six words together.

phrases.english: “Young woman,” “young woman,” “the young woman.”
“Virgin,” “virgins,” “the virgins.”
Two for the laws themselves, one for Abaye's teaching,
phrases.notes: The two basic laws are the אונס and the מפתה.

phrases.english: and one for the gezeira shava.
Two are left over for him.
One, to include those forbidden by prohibitions,
and one, to include those forbidden with karet.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Pooling the sources: all six words are counted together
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each sage uses only one set of three words, so they disagree
steps.terutzMaskana: Both use all six words the same way; the two extra words include girls forbidden by a לאו and by כרת

steps.title: A תנא who limits the fine to a girl he can marry
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's ruling rejects a ברייתא in which two תנאים read ״ולו תהיה לאשה״ as limiting the קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: This excludes the view of a תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: ״And to him she shall be a wife״. שמעון התימני says: a woman with whom קידושין takes effect. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says: a woman who is fit for him to keep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that disagrees with our משנה, and says the משנה comes to reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says even forbidden girls get the קנס. This ברייתא uses the פסוק from step 2 to limit the קנס. שמעון התימני requires that קידושין can take effect, which leaves out women forbidden with כרת. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא requires that he be allowed to stay married to her.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude / reject
A sage of the משנה period
Here: קידושין that takes effect
Fit for him to keep as a wife

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's ruling, that the fine applies even to forbidden girls, was not shared by every תנא.

phrases.english: And this excludes the view of this tanna, as it was taught:
“And to him she shall be a wife,”

phrases.aramaic: שִׁמְעוֹן הַתִּימְנִי אוֹמֵר: אִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ הֲוָיָה.
phrases.english: Shimon HaTimni says: a woman with whom there can be betrothal.
phrases.notes: The word ״תהיה״ (she shall be) hints at הויה, meaning the קידושין actually works.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
a woman who is fit for him to keep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the sources for the משנה, the גמרא names the opinion the משנה rejects
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some תנאים limit the קנס based on ״ולו תהיה לאשה״: either to a woman whose קידושין works, or to a woman he may keep

steps.title: What is the difference between the two תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between שמעון התימני and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which case the two תנאים would rule on differently. This sets up רבי זירא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two wordings sound similar, so the גמרא wants a real case where the outcome changes.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the two views in step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two תנאים would rule differently

steps.title: רבי זירא: a ממזרת or a נתינה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the difference is a ממזרת or a נתינה: קידושין works with them, but he may not keep them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: a ממזרת or a נתינה is the difference between them. For the one who says "a woman with whom there is קידושין", she does have קידושין. For the one who says "fit for him to keep", she is not fit for him to keep.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives the case where the two תנאים disagree: women forbidden only by a לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a ממזרת or a נתינה, קידושין does take effect, so by שמעון התימני the קנס applies. But he is not allowed to stay married to her, so by רבי שמעון בן מנסיא there is no קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman born from a forbidden union
A woman descended from the גבעונים
According to the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: A ממזרת or a נתינה is the dividing case. Her קידושין works, so שמעון התימני says the קנס applies. He may not keep her, so רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says it does not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
A mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman is the difference between them.
According to the one who says there must be betrothal with her,
this one too has betrothal.
According to the one who says she must be fit for him to keep,
this one is not fit for him to keep.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: מַמְזֶרֶת וּנְתִינָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Women forbidden by a לאו, where קידושין works but he may not keep her, such as a ממזרת or a נתינה

steps.title: What is the difference according to רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי עקיבא, קידושין does not take effect with חייבי לאוין, so the ממזרת case no longer shows a difference. What does?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי עקיבא, who says that קידושין does not take effect with women forbidden by a לאו, what is the difference between the two opinions?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer from Step 13. It shows that this answer does not work for רבי עקיבא's view and asks for a different difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said a ממזרת is a case where קידושין works but he may not keep her. רבי עקיבא holds that קידושין does not work at all with someone forbidden by a לאו, and a ממזרת is forbidden by a לאו. So for him, a ממזרת fails both tests, and both תנאים would say no קנס. We need a new case that splits them.

keyTerms.meaning: betrothal takes effect (literally, 'catches')
people forbidden to each other by a simple negative commandment (a לאו)
what is the difference between them?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי עקיבא is arguing with שמעון התימני or רבי שמעון בן מנסיא here. The גמרא is only asking how their argument looks if we also accept רבי עקיבא's rule about קידושין.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Akiva, who said:
Betrothal does not take effect with those forbidden by a negative prohibition,
phrases.notes: A ממזרת is forbidden by a לאו, so for רבי עקיבא, betrothing her does not work.

phrases.english: what is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means שמעון התימני and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא from Step 11.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that Step 13's answer fails according to רבי עקיבא and asks for a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where, according to רבי עקיבא, קידושין works but he may not keep her.

steps.title: The difference is an אלמנה with a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: Even according to רבי עקיבא, the two opinions differ over an אלמנה with a כהן גדול, following רבי סימאי's report of רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: an אלמנה with a כהן גדול, according to רבי סימאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a new case: an אלמנה with a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי סימאי, רבי עקיבא agrees that קידושין works between an אלמנה and a כהן גדול. Even so, he may not keep her. So שמעון התימני would say he pays the קנס, because the קידושין works, and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא would say he does not pay, because she is not fit for him to keep.

keyTerms.meaning: a widow
the High Priest, who may not marry a widow

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
in the case of a widow with a High Priest,
in line with Rabbi Simai,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 by giving a new case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An אלמנה with a כהן גדול: according to רבי סימאי, רבי עקיבא holds that קידושין works there, but he may not keep her.

steps.title: רבי סימאי's report of רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that, according to רבי סימאי, רבי עקיבא does not count the child of an אלמנה and a כהן גדול as a ממזר, because the פסוק calls that child a חלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי סימאי says that רבי עקיבא makes children from all forbidden unions into ממזרים, except for a widow with a כהן גדול. The Torah says, "He shall not take... and he shall not profane," which teaches that he creates חללים, not ממזרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that supports the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah calls the child of a כהן גדול and an אלמנה a חלל and not a ממזר, the union is not treated like the others where קידושין fails. That is why, for רבי עקיבא, קידושין works in this case, which makes it the case where the two opinions differ.

keyTerms.meaning: ממזרים, children of a forbidden union who may not marry into the general community
חללים, children who lose the status of כהונה but are not ממזרים

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the case's status as a forbidden union stays the same. Only its result is different: the child loses כהונה but is not a ממזר.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Simai says:

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַכֹּל עוֹשֶׂה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מַמְזֵרִין,
phrases.english: From all forbidden unions, Rabbi Akiva makes mamzerim,
except for a widow with a High Priest.
For the Torah said:
"He shall not take... and he shall not profane"
he creates chalalim,
but he does not create mamzerim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for following רבי סימאי in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that, for רבי עקיבא, קידושין works between an אלמנה and a כהן גדול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי סימאי, based on the word ״ולא יחלל״.

steps.title: What is the difference according to רבי ישבב?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישבב reports that רבי עקיבא made every child of a forbidden union a ממזר, even from an אלמנה with a כהן גדול. So what difference is left between the two opinions?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי ישבב, who said: "Come, let us cry out against עקיבא בן יוסף, who used to say that the child of anyone who has no permitted relations in Israel is a ממזר," what is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question again, this time according to רבי ישבב's report of רבי עקיבא's view, where the widow case no longer works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ישבב, רבי עקיבא counts even the child of an אלמנה and a כהן גדול as a ממזר. That means קידושין does not work there either. So the answer from Steps 15–16 falls away, and we need yet another case.

keyTerms.meaning: let us cry out (in protest)
a relationship that is permitted within the Jewish people
the child

Come, let us cry out
against Akiva ben Yosef,
phrases.notes: This is רבי עקיבא himself. רבי ישבב protests his view because it makes so many ממזרים.

Anyone who has no permitted relations within Israel,
phrases.notes: He means any forbidden couple, even one forbidden only by a לאו, such as an אלמנה with a כהן גדול.

steps.title: The answer begins: there is a difference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to answer that there is still a difference according to רבי ישבב. The case itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer to Step 17. Only the opening words appear here, and the actual case comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא only says that a difference does exist, even according to רבי ישבב. Keep reading to see which case it names.
